title: JavaScript Testing Applied Check
description: Apply JavaScript testing concepts by choosing appropriate test types, writing assertions, handling async code, using mocks, and avoiding brittle tests.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: The useful test checks the observable output for a specific input.
Use deep equality for object and array contents.

questions.prompt: Which test name is most useful?

options.text: `returns no discount for totals below the threshold`

questions.explanation: A good test name describes the behavior being checked.

options.text: Whether numbers can be stored in variables
Whether the file name contains a dash

questions.explanation: Boundary values such as exactly 18 are important edge cases for comparison logic.

options.text: The test does not return or await the Promise
`then()` can never be used in JavaScript
The test name must be uppercase

questions.explanation: The test runner may finish before the assertion runs unless the Promise is returned or awaited.

questions.prompt: Which Jest test correctly checks that an async function rejects?
questions.explanation: `await expect(promise).rejects...` is the Jest pattern for checking rejected Promises.

questions.prompt: Which dependency is a good candidate to replace with a mock in a regular automated test?

options.text: A network request to a production API
A pure `add(a, b)` function being tested directly
A local variable inside the same function

questions.explanation: External network calls are slow and unpredictable, so tests often replace them with controlled mocks or stubs.

options.text: That the spy or mock was called with those arguments
That an email was definitely delivered to an inbox
That the browser opened a mail app
That the function returned a Promise

questions.explanation: This checks recorded call arguments on a mock or spy. It does not prove real email delivery.

options.text: Checking every private helper call in exact order
Checking the number of blank lines in the source file
Checking the local variable names used inside the function

questions.explanation: Tests that focus on observable behavior are usually less brittle than tests tied to private implementation details.

questions.prompt: What should a regression test for a fixed bug do?

options.text: Fail before the fix and pass after the fix
Only check that the test file exists

questions.explanation: A regression test should capture the buggy behavior so future changes do not reintroduce it.

questions.prompt: Which is the best reason to use `beforeEach()`?

options.text: To create fresh setup needed by each test
To make tests depend on previous tests
To convert all tests to manual tests

questions.explanation: `beforeEach()` is useful for repeated fresh setup while keeping tests independent.

questions.prompt: What is the best interpretation of high code coverage?

options.text: A lot of code ran during tests, but the assertions still need to be meaningful
Every edge case is definitely tested

questions.explanation: Coverage is useful, but it is only a signal. Tests need meaningful assertions and good case selection.

questions.prompt: Which kind of test would best check that a login form works through the browser from typing credentials to seeing the dashboard?
questions.explanation: A full browser workflow is an end-to-end test.

questions.prompt: Which test setup is most independent?

options.text: Each test creates the data it needs or gets fresh data from `beforeEach()`
The second test depends on a user created by the first test
All tests mutate the same global object without resetting it
Tests must run alphabetically to pass

questions.explanation: Independent tests are easier to run, debug, and parallelize.

options.text: Write a failing test, make it pass, then refactor while tests stay passing
Write all production code first and never run tests

questions.explanation: TDD is commonly summarized as red, green, refactor.
